newsitem.title: UK: Brash releases book on NZ's "remarkable reforms".
newsitem.headline: Brash releases book on NZ's "remarkable reforms".

text.p: LONDON, Jan 13 - New Zealand's economic reforms, as seen through the eyes of Reserve Bank governor Don Brash, should be implemented in Britain, according to an English economist.

NZPA reported on Monday that Professor Geoffrey Wood, of City University Business School in London, said Britain and other countries should consider "copying" New Zealand's reforms as outlined in Brash's book, New Zealand's Remarkable Reforms.

Published by the British Institute of Economic Affairs (IEA) and due for release today, the book details the economic decline of New Zealand which sparked deregulation and tough social policies by successive Labour and National governments, and the

In the book, which was based on the 1996 Hayek paper Brash presented to the IEA in June, Brash said the transformation and revival of the New Zealand economy was "one of the most remarkable economic liberalisations of modern times."
In the preface to the 47-page book, Professor Wood said he believed New Zealand should be held up as an example to "policy-makers worldwide".
"It is a lesson from New Zealand not just for the UK, but for the world.
"(In Britain) the Fiscal Responsibility Act would be well worth copying. It embodies some basic principles of responsible fiscal policy, which no government should wish to ignore.

"A depoliticisation of monetary policy's operations, along with political choice of their objective, as is appropriate in a democracy, can be achieved by copying the Reserve Bank Act. It is hard to see why we do not do so," Professor Wood said.
The book will not be released in New Zealand, but copies can be ordered from the IEA.
